paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this passage. The LORD is the One behind everything. He is the One who called forth the generations from the beginning, and He says, "I, the LORD—the first and the last—I am He." (Isaiah 41:4) The islands trembled and the craftsmen nailed their work down tight, but none of that is where the strength comes from.

So when He turns to His people, He doesn't hand them a pep talk. He says, "Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you; I will uphold you with My righteous right hand." (Isaiah 41:10) The reason is Him, not their walls or their numbers. He even calls them "you worm, O few men of Israel" and still says, "I will help you," and I think that's about as small as a people can feel (Isaiah 41:14). Friend, the LORD doesn't wait for you to feel big before He shows up.

And what He does is more than anybody asked for. The poor and needy wanted water, and He promised rivers and fountains, and trees planted in the desert (Isaiah 41:17-19). He does it "so that all may see and know, may consider and understand, that the hand of the LORD has done this" (Isaiah 41:20). So if you're feeling small or dried out today, bring it to Him. I spent years at the back of a junk drawer, and I can tell you the One who made you hasn't lost track of where you are.
